question.text: Two stones are thrown up simultaneously from the edge of a cliff <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>240</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> high with an initial speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively. Which of the following graph best represents the time variation of the relative position of the second stone with respect to the first? (Assume stones do not rebound after hitting the ground and neglect air resistance, take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mi> </mi><msup><mi>ms</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)(the figure are schematic and not drawn to scale)

solution.text: S1=10t-12gt2. When S1=-240⇒t=8s. So, at t=8 seconds first stone will reach the ground. S2=40t-12gt2. Till t=8 s, S2-S1=30t. But after 8 s S1 is constant =-240. Relative to stone 1 for (t1>8) s displacements of stone 2 , S2+240. And at t=12 s seconds stone will reach the ground.
